papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 212 of 249 patients (85.1%) with izalontamab brengitecan and 147 of 248 patients (59.3%) with chemotherapy and were predominantly hematologic. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Izalontamab brengitecan significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC whose disease had progressed after first-line treatment. These findings support izalontamab brengitecan as a new second-line treatment for this population in China. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06304974.

papers.abstract_en: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

papers.abstract_en: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

papers.abstract_en: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after surgery and contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and health-care burden, and are frequently used as endpoints in clinical studies. However, absence of standardised definitions and heterogeneity in component selection limit comparability across studies and might bias estimates of treatment effects. The Postoperative Pulmonary Complications-Evaluation for Consensus on Standardised Outcomes (PrECiSIOn) study was an international, mixed-method consensus study using a Delphi process to establish a standardised definition of PPCs, determine severity-based ranking of individual components, and define approaches for their assessment. A multidisciplinary panel of experts in PPCs was recruited and candidate PPC components were identified through a focused literature review, structured into domains, and evaluated across iterative Delphi rounds using a seven-point Likert scale, with consensus predefined as ≥75% agreement. Patient and patient care representative perspectives were incorporated through interviews and surveys, and panellists assigned severity weights to components reaching consensus. Input from 44 panellists and five patients and patient representatives informed the prioritisation of clinically meaningful outcomes. Consensus was achieved on a standardised PPC construct comprising components grouped into four domains: symptoms, diagnoses, therapies, and outcomes. Panellists supported the use of routinely collected clinical data and a standardised in-hospital monitoring approach but did not reach consensus on the optimal follow-up period or need for post-discharge surveillance. Severity-based rank ordering enabled hierarchical organisation of PPC components according to their clinical importance, supporting the development of ordinal composite outcomes that account for differences in severity between individual complications. This international consensus-based framework provides a standardised definition of PPCs incorporating severity-based rank ordering, addresses important limitations of existing composite outcomes, and might facilitate more consistent and clinically meaningful evaluation of perioperative interventions. Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: With the recent approvals of the FLAURA2 and MARIPOSA regimens in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), identifying clinico-genomic features predictive of suboptimal outcomes with first-line osimertinib monotherapy is critical in guiding upfront treatment selections. METHODS: This is a multicenter retrospective study enrolling patients with advanced NSCLC harboring common EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions [ex19del], L858R) treated with first-line osimertinib monotherapy across 13 centers (Clinical cohort). Comprehensive baseline genomic data on tumor tissue were available for DFCI and MSKCC (Genomic cohort). The association of clinicogenomic features with real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was investigated. Caris Life Science cohort was used for RNA-sequencing analysis. RESULTS: A total of 1488 patients were enrolled in the clinical cohort; at median follow-up of 43.3 months, median rwPFS was 16.3 months (95%CI 15.3-17.4), median overall survival was 36.7 months (95%CI 34.8-39.4). TP53 mutated (TP53MUT) was independently associated with shorter rwPFS compared with TP53 wild-type (TP53WT), specifically in EGFR ex19del (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.68, p<0.001) than in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.18, p=0.2). Using a survROC model for rwPFS, PD-L1 was the variable with greatest impact on risk of progression at 6 (ΔAUC=0.0549) and 12 (ΔAUC=0.0348) months. In the genomic cohort, patients with TSGMUT (RBM10, CREBBP, ATM, RB1, KMT2D, TSC2, PTEN) had shorted rwPFS compared to TSGWT (aHR 1.5, p=0.01), specifically in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.8, p=0.02). Combining TP53 with TSG, pts with TP53MUT plus at least one TSGMUT and pts with TP53WT-TSGMUT had shorter rwPFS compared to TP53WT-TSGWT and TP53MUT-TSGWT. In the genomic cohort, PD-L1 TPS was the strongest predictor of very-early rwPFS (ΔAUC=0.16), followed by TP53-TSG (ΔAUC=0.08). PD-L1 was associated with higher MET mRNA and immunohistochemistry expression and transcriptional program enriched for proliferative, inflammatory, and metabolic signaling pathways. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter real-world cohort, baseline PD-L1 and TP53 combined with TSG predict very-early progression to first-line osimertinib, with EGFR subtype-specific prognostic impact of genomic co-alterations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups. RESEARCH QUESTION: Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation. RESULTS: Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations. INTERPRETATION: Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden. TRIAL REGISTRY: ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Chemoradiotherapy commonly causes radiation-induced lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, as measured by reductions in absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and hemoglobin level (Hb). We aimed to quantify these hematological toxicities and characterize dose-time-response relationships between temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers and radiation exposure to the circulating blood during volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) definitive chemoradiotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Blood biomarker measurements were collected from 93 NSCLC patients, treated between 2018 and 2024, at pre-, during-, and post-treatment time points. Radiotherapy prescription doses were 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 55 Gy in 20 fractions, or 50 Gy in 25 fractions with concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy. Organs at risks were delineated by the TotalSegmentator software. The blood dose-volume histogram was estimated through simulations of blood dynamics using the HEDOS software and VMAT dose accumulation was calculated with the BeamSplitter algorithm. Dose-time-response relationships were modelled by linear and exponentially decaying curves, from which rates of change were extracted and goodness of fit quantified using the R2- value. RESULTS: Baseline blood biomarker values (median ± interquartile range) were (1.8±0.9) × 109/L for ALC, (5.6±3.0) × 109/L for ANC, and 132±19 g/L for Hb. Prior to treatment, 0%, 0%, and 30% of patients exhibited lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, respectively. During treatment, these proportions increased to 71%, 19%, and 77%. Dose-response analysis revealed rates of change at low doses of radiation: -69%/Gy (ALC), -83%/Gy (ANC), and -3%/Gy (Hb), with model fits showing R² values between 0.78 and 0.96. CONCLUSIONS: Hematological toxicities were frequent in NSCLC patients treated with VMAT chemoradiotherapy. Radiation exposure was associated with changes in circulating lymphocyte counts and hemoglobin, supporting prospective investigation into reducing circulating blood dose during chemoradiation to mitigate hematological toxicity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To determine the prevalence of comorbid mental health disorders (MHDs) and association with stage of diagnosis, extent of resection, and post-operative morbidity/mortality in patients undergoing operative intervention for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Adults undergoing elective resection of stage I-III NSCLC were identified from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (July 2018-June 2024) and linked to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to determine long-term survival. Primary outcomes were stage at diagnosis, extent of resection, perioperative morbidity, and 5-year survival. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regressions estimated associations between MHDs on each outcome. Risk-adjusted survival was derived using multivariable frailty Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Among 103,263 patients, 24.4% (n=25,163) had ≥1 MHD. Prevalence of MHDs increased from 16.8% in 2018 to 28.0% in 2024 (p<0.001). In risk-adjusted analysis, patients with an MHD were more likely to have clinical stage I disease (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.22) and to undergo sublobar resection (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). Perioperative mortality, morbidity, and length of stay were all significantly increased in patients with MHDs. In risk-adjusted analysis among Medicare linked patients, 5-year mortality was modestly but significantly greater among patients with MHDs (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18). CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of MHDs among patients undergoing NSCLC resection nearly doubled over 6 years and was associated with an ∼20% increase in morbidity and a reduction in adjusted 5-year survival. These findings underscore the need for targeted perioperative pathways and longitudinal support to mitigate adverse outcomes in this growing population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Without cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, cystic fibrosis is associated with an accelerated decline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of approximately 1·5% per year. Although treatment with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) initially increases ppFEV1, little is known about its subsequent effect on ppFEV1 decline. Recent analyses of the extension phases of the phase 3 ETI pivotal studies found no evidence of ppFEV1 decline over 4 years in patients aged 12 years and older who were treated with ETI. The objective of this study was to examine the decline in ppFEV1 in a large, real-world cohort of adults with cystic fibrosis. METHODS: Data from adults (aged ≥18 years) with cystic fibrosis and at least one F508del CFTR variant who initiated treatment with ETI between Dec 24, 2019, and Dec 23, 2023, at 31 cystic fibrosis centres included in the French prospective national observational ETI study in adults were analysed over 3 years. Eligible participants were those with at least three measures of ppFEV1 taken within 3 months following ETI initiation and the end of follow-up. The reference ppFEV1 was the highest ppFEV1 reached during the first 3 months of ETI treatment, after which subsequent decline in ppFEV1 was analysed by use of a linear mixed-effects model with random effects to estimate each participant's variation from the population mean. FINDINGS: Data from 2321 adults with cystic fibrosis were included in this analysis. 1262 (54·4%) participants were male and 1059 (45·6%) were female. Median age was 29·2 years (IQR 23·1-36·7) and the pre-ETI initiation ppFEV1 was 59·7% (IQR 39·8-79·1). Within the first 3 months following ETI initiation, ppFEV1 increased by a median of 14·5 percentage points (IQR 7·9-22·7). The subsequent mean decline in ppFEV1 was 0·70% (95% CI 0·57-0·83) per year. Importantly, the decline in ppFEV1 was heterogeneous, with 1583 (68·2%) of 2321 participants showing no or limited decline (less than or equal to 1·5% per year). The remaining 738 (31·8%) participants showed a decline of greater than 1·5% per year, with 342 (46·3%) of these participants having a decline of greater than 3·0% per year. In multivariable analyses, the decline in ppFEV1 was greater in participants with a higher ppFEV1 at 3 months after ETI initiation. Treatment with oral azithromycin at 1 year after ETI initiation was associated with a lower risk of having a decline greater than 1·5% per year (relative risk 0·78 [95% CI 0·68-0·90]; p <0·01), as was treatment with inhaled antibiotics (0·81 [0·70-0·94]; p <0·01). INTERPRETATION: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies. papers.abstract_en: The optimal integration of immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in neoadjuvant treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We integrate paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell RNA sequencing and TCR sequencing data from patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT), chemoradiotherapy (NCRT), or immuno-chemoradiotherapy (NICRT) to investigate how these regimens shape intratumoral CD8+ T cell responses. Favorable responses to NICT are associated with maintenance of pre-existing CXCL13+PD-1+ CD8+ T cells and post-treatment enrichment of a progenitor-like CD8Tex_CXCR4 subset. In contrast, CRT responders show reduced CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells and enrichment of clonally expanded, cytotoxic PD-1- CD8Teff_NIBAN1 cells. These divergent programs are validated in public datasets and independent prospective cohorts. In murine models, radiotherapy limits PD-1+ T cell expansion, whereas induction anti-PD-1 treatment followed by radiotherapy improves tumor control. Together, these findings reveal distinct CD8+ T cell programs associated with response to different neoadjuvant modalities and provide a cellular rationale for optimizing immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. RESEARCH QUESTION: Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. RESULTS: Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. INTERPRETATION: Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a common malignant tumor in China, with a poor five-year survival rate due to the lack of effective early diagnostic methods. This study aimed to identify potential non-invasive biomarkers and clarify their underlying mechanisms. METHODS: We employed an integrative approach combining serum proteomic profiling, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analyses. Quantitative proteomics was conducted on 15 serum samples of treatment-naive early-stage ESCC patients and 5 from healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were cross-referenced with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from the GSE53624 dataset, and a diagnostic model was developed using LASSO regression. Cross-validation was performed using scRNA-seq data. The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was utilized to validate FTL in 155 serum samples from two centers. In silico FTL knockouts were conducted using scTenifoldKnk, followed by GO, KEGG, and PPI network analyses. RESULTS: Proteomic profiling identified a total of 129 DEPs. Intersection with GSE53624 DEGs yielded 8 overlapping genes, and a 6-biomarker (TF, CHAD, CSRP1, FCGR3A, RCN1, FTL) diagnostic model was built, with AUC 0.882-1.0 across validation cohorts. scRNA-seq intersection analysis identified FTL as the only overlapping DEG, exhibiting high expression levels in ESCC epithelial cells and macrophages. FTL demonstrated strong standalone diagnostic performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.872 to 0.970 across three GEO datasets. ELISA validation yielded an AUC of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.674-0.816) and 0.838 (95% CI: 0.751-0.905) for early-stage ESCC, surpassing the performance of CEA and SCCA. The combination of FTL with SCCA further enhanced discriminatory efficacy. Mechanistically, FTL was associated with altered immune cell infiltration, characterized by increased resting dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and decreased follicular helper T cells, as well as activation of the ferroptosis pathway. In silico FTL knockouts revealed DEGs enriched in stress and metabolic biological processes, extracellular vesicles (cellular component), transcriptional regulation (molecular function, CHOP-ATF3 complex), IL-17/TNF pathways, and lipid/ROS-related pathways. Protein-protein interaction hubs included FOS, ATF3, NFKBIA, and CXCL8, with FTL linked to NFE2L2, TFRC, and TXNRD1. CONCLUSIONS: FTL represents a credible non-invasive serum diagnostic biomarker for ESCC. Computational analyses suggest it is a candidate molecule requiring further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a disease that is difficult to diagnose because its clinical findings are nonspecific and it carries high mortality when not treated early. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), the gold standard for diagnosis, cannot be performed in every patient because of contraindications related to contrast medium; Noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT), on the other hand, cannot be used as a reliable tool for exclusion because of its low sensitivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the paired images of 716 patients (129 PE-positive, 587 PE-negative) who had undergone both CTPA and NCCT on the same day between 2018 and 2026 were examined. The availability of two scans obtained from the same patient on the same day provided a paired cohort in which clinical and anatomical variables other than the presence of contrast were largely held constant, so that the CTPA scan established with certainty where a thrombus lay in each patient whose noncontrast scan was analyzed. Each scan was converted into a 12-second mediastinal-window video, from which a 40-frame segment centered on the temporal midpoint of the recording was extracted for analysis. For the automatic detection of thrombus, three-dimensional deep learning architectures have been developed: PureStream-3D, BiLSTM-ResNet-3D based on bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and AttnFocus-3D based on an attention mechanism. The models have been optimized with different training configurations to address class imbalance, and the dataset has been divided at the patient level into 70% training, 20% validation, and 10% independent test sets. RESULTS: In the CTPA test set, the highest discrimination has been achieved by the AttnFocus-3D-1 model (accuracy 0.9306; area under the curve [AUC] 0.98), whereas the most balanced sensitivity-specificity profile has been obtained with the BiLSTM-ResNet-3D-2 variant (sensitivity 0.9138, specificity 0.8571). In the NCCT test set, the AttnFocus-3D-2 architecture has reached an accuracy of 0.9306, an AUC of 0.97, a sensitivity of 0.9655, and a specificity of 0.7857. CONCLUSION: Taken together, these findings indicate that the developed deep learning approaches are strong in confirming the presence or absence of PE and can be considered as a decision-support infrastructure in clinical scenarios with high diagnostic uncertainty.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab with/without 2 cycles of chemotherapy has been approved for untreated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in Japan, based on CheckMate 9LA and CheckMate 227, but long-term real-world data in Japanese patients are limited. METHODS: LIGHT-NING is an ongoing, multicenter, observational study, examining nivolumab plus ipilimumab, with/without chemotherapy for patients with stage IV or recurrent NSCLC. We assessed treatment patterns, effectiveness, and safety, using 2.5-year data from November 2020 to June 2024. Exploratory analyses characterized early progressive disease (PD) and associated baseline factors. These analyses were hypothesis-generating in nature. RESULTS: Of 545 patients (median age: 70 years, 18.9% female, 89.9% Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, median follow-up period 15.1 months), 319 (58.5%) received nivolumab plus ipilimumab with chemotherapy and 226 (41.5%) without chemotherapy. Median overall survival and real-world progression-free survival were 21.7 and 6.8 months, respectively, in patients with chemotherapy, and 18.8 and 6.3 months, respectively, without chemotherapy. Grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 170 (53.3%) and 69 (30.5%) patients, respectively. As an exploratory analysis, early PD in the cohort without chemotherapy was associated with body mass index in squamous cell carcinoma and albumin, lactate dehydrogenase, and lung immune prognostic index in non-squamous cell carcinoma. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis of LIGHT-NING study indicated that safety and effectiveness in Japanese patients were consistent with those observed in CheckMate 9LA and CheckMate 227. No new safety signals were observed, the combination therapy was generally well manageable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung protective ventilation is crucial for preventing ventilator-induced lung injury in cardiac surgery. The protective role of a low tidal volume (VT) has been established, whereas the added protection afforded by lung recruitment remains uncertain. We investigated whether sigh breaths could provide additional lung protection, when added to protective ventilation with low VT. METHODS: This randomized, assessor-blinded, phase 2 proof-of-concept trial enrolled 192 patients undergoing elective on-pump cardiac surgery from February to August 2024. Patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive sigh ventilation (sigh breaths plus protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients) or conventional ventilation (protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients). Sigh breaths targeting a plateau pressure of 35 cmH2O (or 40 cmH2O for BMI >35 kg/m2) were delivered once every 6 min. Perioperative respiratory mechanics and gas exchange were monitored. The primary outcome was postoperative oxygenation, a marker of lung injury, as measured by the time-weighted average SpO2/FiO2 ratio during the first postextubation hour. There were 9 predefined secondary outcomes, including the severity of respiratory failure within postextubation day 7. RESULTS: All 192 patients completed the trial (53% male; median age, 64 [55-72] years). Perioperatively, sigh ventilation produced sustained improvements in oxygenation and respiratory system compliance, together with reductions in driving pressure and mechanical power (All P interaction<0.001). After extubation, the mean time-weighted SpO2/FiO2 ratio was higher in the sigh ventilation group (380 ± 86 vs 338 ± 93; mean difference 42.1, 95% CI [16.7 to 67.5]; P=0.001). The severity and occurrence of respiratory failure was reduced in the sigh ventilation group compared with conventional ventilation group (common odds ratio for lower severity 2.2; 95% CI [1.2 to 3.8]; P=0.007). There was no difference in adverse events of interest between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, adding sigh breaths was safe and resulted in a statistically significant improvement in postoperative oxygenation. Nevertheless, the clinical importance of this finding is uncertain because oxygenation was adequately maintained in both groups. Reduction in driving pressure and mechanical power, together with findings in secondary outcomes, suggest additional lung protection and justify future trials. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06248320); registered on January 30, 2024.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Spark-like T cells constitute a novel functional state of CD8+T cells and have emerged as key drivers of immunotherapy response in preclinical models, yet their clinical relevance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains undefined. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE207422), spatial transcriptomics (GSE271689), bulk RNA expression cohorts (TCGA-NSCLC, GSE37745, GSE41271, and GSE72094), and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) of a 100-patient cohort treated with anti-PD-1 were integrated to characterize Spark-like T cells and assess their clinical relevance. A 14-gene prognostic signature was constructed via LASSO-Cox regression. RESULTS: Spark-like T cells were significantly enriched in anti-PD-1 responders in the single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. mIHC validation in the 100-patient cohort confirmed that high Spark-like T cell intensity in tumors was independently associated with prolonged overall survival (log-rank test, p < 0.001) and partial response to anti-PD-1 therapy (p = 0.0075). Spatial transcriptomics indicated strong co-localization of Spark-like T cells with M1 macrophages (Spearman r = 0.524, p = 3.4 × 10-42), suggesting their spatial co-enrichment with pro-inflammatory myeloid cells. In silico knockout identified TNF, ENTPD1 (CD39), and IL2 as cooperative regulators of Spark-like T cell effector function. The 14-gene Spark-like T cell-related signature (VDAC1, ITGB1, GALNT2, SEMA7A, UBB, SLC7A5, FURIN, SNX9, PSMB2, CXCL13, TOX, PPM1M, CCND2, and CLNK) robustly predicted overall survival across all four independent cohorts and remained an independent prognostic factor after adjustment for age, sex, and tumor stage. High-risk patients exhibited an immune-excluded, oncogene-driven tumor microenvironment with reduced infiltration of CD8+T cells. CONCLUSIONS: Spark-like T cells are clinically relevant determinants of anti-PD-1 response in NSCLC. mIHC quantification and the 14-gene signature provide promising translational tools for patient stratification and risk assessment.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pulmonology, University Hospital of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the right atrial pressure to cardiac output relationship (RAP/CO-slope) from rest to end exercise in patients undergoing exercise right heart catheterization for suspected or confirmed pulmonary hypertension (PH). METHODS: The analysis used data from the retrospective arm of the Pulmonary Hemodynamics during Exercise Network (PEX NET), a multicenter collaboration involving 23 PH centers. Patients were included if resting and exercise measurements were obtained in the same body position and if RAP/CO-slopes were available. Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age, sex, and hemoglobin were applied. Time dependent ROC curves were used to identify a prognostic cut off. RESULTS: A total of 856 patients were included (median age 59 years; 67% female), of whom 336 had PH. Over a median follow up of 6.5 years, 114 patients (13%) died. Higher RAP/CO-slopes were independently associated with increased mortality, even after adjusting for established resting and exercise hemodynamics (hazard ratio 1.08, 95%CI: 1.03-1.13, p < 0.001). Among patients with manifest PH at rest, a RAP/CO-slope ≥1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was linked to a 2.2 fold higher mortality risk (hazard ratio: 2.20; 95% CI: 1.1-4.5; p = 0.032) compared with slopes <1.0 mmHg·min·L⁻¹. In a multivariable model including NT proBNP, 6 minute walking distance, and WHO functional class, the RAP/CO-slope remained the strongest predictor of mortality. CONCLUSION: The RAP/CO-slope is a strong, independent prognostic marker across a spectrum of RV afterload stress. A RAP/CO slope ≥1 mmHg·min·L⁻¹ was identified as particularly predictive in manifest PH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are widely used for postoperative acute pain management. However, the safety and efficacy of postoperative scheduled oral ibuprofen remain unclear in children. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of scheduled ibuprofen combined with diclofenac suppository for postoperative analgesia in children following the Nuss procedure for pectus excavatum. METHODS: Sixty patients who underwent the Nuss procedure from September 2024 to August 2025 were randomly divided and assigned to either the experimental or control group. The experimental group received scheduled ibuprofen combined with a diclofenac suppository, whereas the control group received a diclofenac suppository and ibuprofen on demand. The postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) scores, supplemental opioid consumption, time to first ambulation, length of hospital stay, and incidence of adverse events were recorded for both groups. RESULTS: The VAS scores at 6-24 h postoperatively were significantly lower for the experimental group than the control group (p < 0.05). The experimental group required less opioids than the control group (62.4 ± 5.7 vs. 67.5 ± 6.4 µg, p = 0.002; difference: -5.167 µg, 95% confidence interval: -8.325 to -2.008). Additionally, the time to first ambulation (5.9 ± 0.6 vs. 6.4 ± 0.7 h, p = 0.005; difference: -0.486 h, 95% confidence interval: -0.924 to -0.076) and length of hospital stay (6.8 ± 0.8 vs. 7.3 ± 0.8 days, p = 0.022; difference: -0.500 days, 95% confidence interval: -0.924 to -0.076) were shorter for the experimental group than the control group. The incidence of adverse events was similar for both groups (p > 0.05). CONCLUSION: This study indicates that scheduled ibuprofen combined with diclofenac suppository provides effective analgesia following the Nuss procedure, reduces opioid consumption, and promotes recovery. No serious NSAID-related adverse events were observed during the short postoperative observation period. However, the study was not powered to establish safety or exclude clinically important differences in uncommon adverse events. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2400089927.

papers.abstract_en: To determine the cancer-initiating activity of oncoprotein CIP2A, which is overexpressed in a majority of cancers and promotes cell growth by stabilizing MYC, we established an alveolar type 2 cell-specific CIP2A transgenic mouse line. Among 114 transgenic mice aged 12 months or older, 23 (20.2%) developed lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)-like disease, significantly higher than in the control mice (3/63, 4.8%). Multi-omic studies revealed enrichment of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway in tumor tissues from transgenic mice. CIP2A upregulated phosphorylation of FOXO3A (p-FOXO3A S253) by inhibiting phosphatase PP2A-B56α and promoted FOXO3A mitochondrial translocation. CIP2A-FOXO3A reshaped mitochondrial morphology, activated mitochondrial DNA transcription, and enhanced complexes IV/V activities. OXPHOS inhibitor repressed CIP2A-induced cell proliferation and tumor growth. Moreover, tobacco carcinogens upregulated CIP2A and p-FOXO3A S253 and significantly increased cancer incidence in CIP2A-transgenic mice. These data indicate that CIP2A plays a critical role in mitochondrial regulation and represents a promising therapeutic target for LUADs lacking actionable driver mutations.

papers.abstract_en: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: In the United States, tuberculosis (TB) incidence rates are substantially higher among racial/ethnic minorities compared with non-Hispanic White persons. However, few analyses have investigated the mechanisms driving these disparities. OBJECTIVES: To assess the contribution of geographic factors and individual TB risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in TB incidence among U.S.-born individuals. METHODS: We analyzed TB case data for 2012-2019 from the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System, stratified by race/ethnicity, age, sex, and Public Use Microdata Area (PUMA). Age-sex standardized incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were calculated to quantify disparities across racial/ethnic groups. We decomposed these IRRs to quantify the contribution of differences within and between PUMAs to overall disparities. We also estimated the contributions of racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of established TB risk factors-diagnosed diabetes, current smoking, HIV infection, and excess alcohol use-to TB disparities. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native and non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander persons had the highest TB incidence rates compared to non-Hispanic White persons (IRR: 15.3 (95% CI: 12.5, 18.6) and 18.1 (12.3, 26.2) respectively). Within-PUMA TB incidence differences accounted for most of the differences in incidence by race/ethnicity, representing 52-96% of total IRRs for each racial/ethnic population. Racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of individual risk factors had minimal impact on total TB incidence disparities. CONCLUSIONS: Eliminating racial/ethnic disparities in TB will require more than addressing individual risk factors. Combatting structural or community-level determinants of TB, including treating infection to prevent disease, will be important for accelerating TB elimination.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) contributes substantially to global morbidity and mortality, while suboptimal inhaled medication adherence worsens clinical outcomes. Existing evidence confirms disease knowledge shapes self-medication behaviors, yet it remains unclear which distinct COPD knowledge domains correlate with adherence improvements following standardized patient education. OBJECTIVE: To explore associations between changes in each domain of COPD-related knowledge and variations in inhaled medication adherence following routine outpatient standardized health education. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a multicenter, prospective, observational pre-post study. Consecutive stable COPD outpatients aged ≥ 40 years were recruited between June 2024 and June 2025 from two tertiary hospitals in Chongqing, China. METHODS: All participants received 30-minute standardized education covering all 13 knowledge subdomains of the Bristol COPD Knowledge Questionnaire (BCKQ). BCKQ, Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS), and COPD Assessment Test (CAT) were administered at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Spearman correlation and ANCOVA with Holm-Bonferroni correction were used; two supplementary sensitivity models were applied to verify result stability. RESULTS: A total of 894 patients were included in the final analysis. Scores of the total BCKQ, MARS, and CAT all showed statistically significant changes after education (all P < 0.001). Among all 13 knowledge subdomains, only increased epidemiological knowledge scores were positively correlated with improved inhaled medication adherence (ρ = 0.43, P < 0.001). After adjusting for baseline adherence, total baseline knowledge and multiple demographic/clinical confounders, elevated epidemiological knowledge was independently associated with higher follow-up MARS scores (B = 0.33, SE = 0.04, P < 0.001). Consistent statistical significance for ΔEpidemiology was observed across two sensitivity analytical models. Baseline low adherence was 64.0%, and medication-related knowledge gains were not associated with adherence change. CONCLUSION: Improvements in COPD epidemiological knowledge were independently associated with greater inhaled medication adherence after standardized outpatient education. Prioritizing education on disease progression and long-term threats may be an effective strategy to optimize adherence in busy clinical settings.

papers.abstract_en: Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

papers.abstract_en: Intrinsic resistance of small cell lung cancer (SCLC) to immunotherapy underscores our limited understanding of how tumors can evade immune responses. Here we demonstrated that neural cell adhesion molecule 1 (NCAM1, also called CD56) facilitates disease progression, tumor stemness, and resistance to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in SCLC. Mechanistically, cis-binding of NCAM1 with its ligand L1CAM on the surface of identical tumor cell occupied considerable antigenic epitopes of L1CAM, and thereby prevented L1CAM from trans-binding with CD56+ NK cells to form immune-synapse structures, which may render the tumor cells more resistant to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in SCLC. Additionally, CHMP4B, a member of the ESCRT complex involved in plasma membrane repair, were essential for SCLC stemness and NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and NCAM1 can protect SCLC cells from immune attack and stem cell renewal by interacting with CHMP4B. SCLC specimens with concurrent high expression of NCAM1 and CHMP4B exhibited lower cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, were located farther from cytotoxic immune cells, and were associated with inferior clinical outcomes. These findings reveal potential mechanisms of NCAM1 in sustaining SCLC stemness and resisting cytolytic attack, and provide a potential target of CHMP4B against self-renewal and immunoresistance.

papers.abstract_en: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and malignant pleural disease (MPD) are common complications of cancer. Although they may significantly affect the quality of life, treatment options remain limited. Official guidelines recommend effusion drainage and pleurodesis, and, while they may achieve symptomatic relief, their impact on disease progression is limited. Intrapleural therapy has been studied for several decades due to its theoretical (and proven) superior local drug retention, maximising drug exposure. Recent works on intrapleural administration include exploring novel therapeutic agents and administration methods, such as hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITHOC) and pressurised intrathoracic chemotherapy (PITAC). These therapies directly modulate the tumour environments. Promising intrapleural candidates include targeted and immunotherapies such as CAR (chimeric antigen receptor)-T cells, PD-1 (programmed death protein 1) inhibitors, and IL-6 (interleukin-6) inhibitors. However, the level of evidence remains mixed, requiring further studies and quantitative synthesis.

papers.abstract_en: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

papers.abstract_en: Severe asthma is increasingly managed with endotype-guided biologics, yet a clinically important subgroup remains corticosteroid-dependent, repeatedly exacerbating, or unable to achieve durable multidomain remission. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered cells offer a qualitatively different therapeutic logic: recognition of a cellular compartment can be coupled to selective depletion, localized regulation, or payload delivery, potentially enabling finite immune reprogramming rather than continuous mediator blockade. This Review asks under what conditions that added biological risk could be justified in asthma. We classify evidence into four proximity tiers-direct asthma preclinical evidence, patient-derived ex vivo or disease-adjacent preclinical evidence, human clinical evidence in other immune-mediated diseases, and broader platform evidence-and use this hierarchy to support explicit go/no-go judgments rather than catalogue constructs. Direct asthma studies support lung-directed CAR-regulatory T cells, IL-5/IL-5Rα-directed cytotoxic strategies, multifunctional type 2 pathway control, and allergen-specific CAR-Tregs; clinical efficacy in asthma has not been established. We propose a target-function-patient framework organized around four mandatory gates: clinical necessity, mechanistic coherence, targetability, and reversibility planning. Targets should be prioritized by pathogenic necessity and physiological dispensability; the cellular chassis and receptor program should be chosen according to the required biological function; and treatment should be restricted to biomarker-defined patients whose residual disease burden justifies living-cell therapy. In asthma, maximal cytotoxicity and indefinite persistence are not default virtues. The most plausible initial role is a narrow, biologic-refractory population in whom a controllable, mechanistically verified intervention can durably interrupt a disease-maintaining cellular circuit while preserving host defense and tissue repair.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) and Tuberculosis (TB) are both highly prevalent in India, and the combination of both has emerged as a syndemic in the country. Accordingly, the aim was to estimate the pooled prevalence of DM among TB patients in India and identify its predictors. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted, and the data were extracted until 6th May 2025, utilising three databases: PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus. A total of 22 articles were included in the review, and they underwent quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), the Modified-NOS, and the National Institute of Health (NIH) quality assessment tool. The pooled prevalence of DM among TB patients was estimated with a 95% Confidence Interval (CI), assuming potential heterogeneity, as determined by a random-effects model. The predictors were analysed quantitatively, and the pooled adjusted odds ratios (AOR) were estimated. RESULTS: A total of 67,155 individuals were included, ranging from 31 in Maharashtra to 47,831 in Odisha. The pooled prevalence of DM in TB patients was 20% (95% CI: 15%-27%), with the highest prevalence of 30% (95% CI: 17%-45%) observed in Pulmonary-TB cases, compared to all TB cases (18%, 95% CI: 12%-24%). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across the included studies, with I2 = 99.44%, z = 11.80, p < 0.001, suggesting cautious interpretation of the pooled estimate. The predictors reported by the included studies were categorised into seven broad themes. For the male gender, the pooled AOR was 1.35 (95% CI: 0.91-2.01); for advancing age > 40 years, it was statistically significant at p < 0.001, with a pooled AOR of 5.09 (95% CI: 2.97-8.72); for alcoholism, the pooled AOR was 2.33 (95% CI: 0.68-7.96); for smoking, it was 1.10 (95% CI: 0.67-1.81). The pooled AOR for Pulmonary-TB was 1.84 (95% CI: 1.36-2.49) and was statistically significant at p < 0.001. CONCLUSION: The study estimated that one in every fifth TB patient is Diabetic in India, with regional variations; however, substantial heterogeneity suggests cautious interpretation of the pooled estimate. Bidirectional screening and integrated disease management must be mandated at all levels of healthcare to manage this syndemic.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To examine the independent and combined associations of childhood and adulthood stressful life events (SLEs) with lung disease among Chinese adults aged ≥45 years. METHODS: Using CHARLS data (2011-2018), we conducted cross-sectional analysis of baseline (n=10,705) for prevalent lung disease, and longitudinal analysis (n=7,770, 7-year follow-up) for incident lung disease. SLEs were categorized as none, childhood-only, adulthood-only, or both. BMI was categorized according to Chinese adult criteria. Outcomes were self-reported physician-diagnosed lung disease. RESULTS: In cross-sectional analysis, compared with no SLEs, the adjusted odds of prevalent lung disease were higher for childhood-only SLEs (OR=1.35, 95% CI: 1.13 ∼ 1.62), adulthood-only SLEs (OR=1.24, 95% CI: 1.03 ∼ 1.50), and combined childhood and adulthood SLEs (OR=1.53, 95% CI: 1.26 ∼ 1.86). In longitudinal analysis, the adjusted hazards of incident lung disease were higher for childhood-only SLEs (HR=1.29, 95% CI: 1.10 ∼ 1.53) and combined childhood and adulthood SLEs (HR=1.61, 95% CI: 1.35 ∼ 1.93); adulthood-only SLEs were not significantly associated with incident lung disease (HR=1.12, 95% CI: 0.94 ∼ 1.34, P=0.199). CONCLUSION: Childhood SLEs, alone or combined with adulthood SLEs, were associated with higher odds prevalent lung disease and higher hazards of incident lung disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, suggesting that early-life stress may be associated with long-term respiratory health.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Liver metastasis relies on the establishment of a pre-metastatic niche (PMN) before tumor cell seeding. Although low-dose irradiation can modulate local immune responses, whether prophylactic low-dose liver irradiation influences hepatic PMN formation and metastatic colonization remains unclear. METHODS: We used a prophylactic low-dose liver irradiation strategy in mouse models of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) liver metastasis to evaluate its effects on metastatic colonization and hepatic immune remodelling. Bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in vitro functional assays were performed to characterize irradiation-induced hepatocyte-monocyte signaling, and in vivo CXCL10 neutralization was used to assess its functional relevance. RESULTS: Prophylactic low-dose liver irradiation suppressed NSCLC liver metastasis and reshaped the hepatic immune microenvironment during PMN formation. A single 2 Gy dose showed the strongest antimetastatic effect. Mechanistically, 2 Gy irradiation induced hepatocyte-derived SAA1. SAA1 activated a TLR2-NF-κB/RELA-associated transcriptional program in inflammatory monocytes, leading to SLC7A11 upregulation, improved redox homeostasis, and increased CXCL10 secretion. SLC7A11 activity was required to sustain this chemokine-secretory phenotype. CXCL10 neutralization in vivo reduced CD8 + T-cell recruitment and attenuated the antimetastatic effect of low-dose irradiation. CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic low-dose liver irradiation limits NSCLC liver metastasis and is associated with reprogramming of the PMN toward an anti-metastatic immune state. These findings link irradiation to metastatic niche immune remodeling and highlight the translational relevance of low-dose immune radiobiology in metastasis control.

papers.abstract_en: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier and refractory hypoxemia. Despite advances in supportive care, effective targeted therapies remain lacking. A major challenge to therapeutic success is the marked heterogeneity of ARDS, in which distinct biological mechanisms may drive different etiologies, inflammatory subphenotypes, and disease stages. Increasing evidence suggests that alveolar epithelial cells (AECs) are not merely passive targets of injury but active regulators of immune responses. Dynamic interactions between AECs and macrophages, neutrophils, and lymphocytes occur throughout the course of ARDS and contribute to inflammatory amplification, tissue repair, and aberrant remodeling. In this review, we summarize epithelial-immune interaction patterns across the inflammatory exudative, proliferative repair, and fibrotic phases of ARDS. We further discuss how disease stage transitions, immunometabolic regulation, and ARDS heterogeneity shape these interaction networks. Based on these findings, we present an AEC-centered dynamic reprogramming framework that organizes current evidence on how epithelial-immune interactions change during ARDS progression. We also discuss candidate biomarkers, approaches for clinical stage and phenotype identification, therapeutic opportunities, and current evidence limitations, aiming to provide a conceptual framework for stage-specific and precision interventions in ARDS. We further contextualize existing and controversial immunomodulatory strategies, including corticosteroids and IL-6/IL-1 blockade, within this dynamic framework to illustrate how disease stage and patient phenotype may influence therapeutic responses. Throughout the review, we distinguish evidence derived from experimental models from observational data in human ARDS and separately identify human interventional evidence and therapies supported by current clinical guidelines.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids as adjuvant therapy for Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) in patients positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). METHODS: Clinical randomized controlled trials or clinical controlled trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of glucocorticoids as adjuvant therapy for PCP in patients who are HIV-positive were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Data extraction and methodological quality assessment were performed for eligible studies. Meta-analysis and systematic evaluation were conducted using RevMan v.5.1 and STATA v.12.0 software. RESULTS: Nine articles (13 studies) were included. Compared with the controls, patients treated with glucocorticoids had significantly lower mortality rates (OR = 0.41, 95% CI [0.28-0.59], P < 0.00001), early deterioration rates (OR = 0.08, 95% CI [0.02-0.39], P = 0.002), and lower mechanical ventilation rates (OR = 0.32, 95% CI [0.19-0.55], P < 0.0001). Regarding safety, the incidence of adverse effects did not differ significantly between the two groups (OR = 0.74, 95% CI [0.33-1.70], P = 0.48). CONCLUSION: Adjuvant glucocorticoid therapy significantly reduces mortality, early deterioration, and mechanical ventilation rates in patients who are HIV-positive with PCP without increasing adverse reactions. Glucocorticoids may serve as a viable adjuvant treatment option for PCP in patients who are HIV-positive. papers.title_en: Association of trilaciclib use with hematologic outcomes during perioperative immunochemotherapy in resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a prospective observational cohort study.
papers.authors: He C, Lin X, Xu H, Lin J, Li P, Wang W, Chen B, Lin R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, Shantou, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative immunochemotherapy is a key treatment strategy for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) may compromise treatment delivery. Trilaciclib, a transiently acting, reversible cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor, has shown myeloprotective effects in advanced solid tumors; however, evidence in perioperative ESCC is limited. This study investigated the association between trilaciclib use and hematologic outcomes during perioperative immunochemotherapy. METHODS: In this single-center, prospective observational cohort study, 93 patients (control group, n = 65; trilaciclib group, n = 28) enrolled between October 2023 and March 2026 were analyzed. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Binary, longitudinal, and survival outcomes were analyzed using IPTW-weighted Firth-penalized logistic regression, weighted generalized estimating equations, and weighted Cox models, respectively, with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: After weighting, baseline characteristics were well balanced (all standardized mean differences <0.10). Compared with control, the trilaciclib group had lower weighted incidences of grade 3-4 CIM (3.0% vs. 31.2%; odds ratio [OR] 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.48; FDR-adjusted P = 0.007), grade 3-4 neutropenia (3.0% vs. 28.3%; OR 0.12, 95% CI: 0.01-0.55; FDR-adjusted P = 0.010), and grade 3-4 anemia (0.0% vs. 17.3%; OR 0.08, 95% CI: <0.01-0.67; FDR-adjusted P = 0.030). Grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia, severe neutropenia, and febrile neutropenia did not differ significantly. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) use was also lower in the trilaciclib group (34.4% vs. 79.7% and 3.7% vs. 29.6%; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001 and P = 0.010, respectively). Overall survival, disease-free survival, and pathologic outcomes did not differ significantly. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or noninferiority. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center cohort, trilaciclib use was associated with lower grade 3-4 myelosuppression and less hematopoietic supportive care. No statistically significant unfavorable differences in pathologic or survival outcomes were observed; however, equivalence cannot be inferred. These results are hypothesis-generating and require validation in randomized trials.

papers.title_en: Real-world treatment patterns and outcomes in severe acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an observational study.
papers.authors: Árvai-Horváth L, Manzel P, Méhész I, Wessják D, Karádi DÁ, Baglyas S, Lorx A, Valkó L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Doctoral College, Semmelweis University, Üllői Út 26.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) represents a significant healthcare burden. Acute exacerbation (AECOPD) episodes frequently require hospitalization, and a number of these involve intensive care (ICU) unit admission. Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) use is associated with superior outcome, despite this, real-world data indicate that NIV remains underutilized. Our aim was to characterize NIV utilization for severe AECOPD patients admitted to participating Hungarian ICUs. METHODS: We conducted a 2-month long prospective observational study of AECOPD patients in ICUs and collected national health registry data for parallel validation. RESULTS: In five participating ICUs 27 (4.86%) out of 555 screened patients were recruited. Patients were predominantly older, overweight, and had several comorbidities. Hypercapnia, elevated bicarbonate levels and pneumonia were common at admission. ICU mortality was 22.2%, and in-hospital mortality rate reached 37%, compared to a predicted 55 (25-73%) ICU mortality. NIV was used in most patients, however, only 25.9% received NIV exclusively. NIV was the initial ventilation type in 55.6% of cases, but early NIV failure rate was 46.7%. Difficult weaning was reported in 30% of patients. NIV failure was associated with longer ICU stay and increased hospital mortality. National Health Fund data confirmed overall low NIV use, with only 4.8% of COPD patients receiving this therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Severe AECOPD in Hungarian ICUs is currently associated with low NIV utilization, high NIV failure rate and considerable hospital mortality. Future studies should focus on appropriate patient selection, initial NIV application and therapy optimization.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the main subtype of lung cancers and is characterized by metabolic reprogramming and vasculogenic mimicry (VM), both of which contribute to tumor aggressiveness. Although N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) was implicated in NSCLC progression, its involvement in VM remains to be investigated. The aim of this study was to reveal the role of NDRG1 in VM within NSCLC. METHODS: NDRG1 expression and prognostic relevance were analyzed using public databases and NSCLC tissue samples. NSCLC cell lines were used for NDRG1 knockdown or overexpression experiments. Cell proliferative capacity was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, whereas cell motility and invasiveness were determined by Transwell-based assays Metabolic changes were assessed by detecting lactate, triglyceride, cholesterol levels, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR). VM was evaluated by CD34/PAS staining and VM-related protein expression. Wnt/β-catenin signaling was examined by Western blot, immunofluorescence, and a β-catenin inhibitor treatment. RESULTS: NDRG1 expression was markedly elevated in NSCLC and was related to unfavorable prognosis and increased vasculogenic mimicry (VM). NDRG1 silencing suppressed glycolysis, lipid accumulation, cell proliferation, EMT, and angiogenic marker expression. Mechanistically, NDRG1 enhanced β-catenin nuclear translocation and activated Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Inhibition of β-catenin attenuated NDRG1-induced metabolic reprogramming and VM. CONCLUSION: NDRG1 facilitates NSCLC progression by activating Wnt/β-catenin signaling, thereby inducing metabolic reprogramming and VM. These findings suggest that the NDRG1/β-catenin axis may warrant further investigation as a potential therapeutic target in NSCLC, although its therapeutic relevance requires in vivo validation.

papers.abstract_en: Current chemotherapy options for lung cancer (LC) are limited by poor tumor selectivity, systemic toxicity, and acquired resistance. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers a promising minimally invasive modality as a potential conservative or complementary approach, yet its clinical adoption has been constrained by suboptimal photosensitizers and unclear mechanisms. This study investigated a novel PDT regimen combining a 450 nm blue laser with the photosensitizer sinoporphyrin sodium (DVDMS) to address these limitations in LC. Our findings demonstrate that BL-DVDMS treatment selectively inhibits lung cancer cell proliferation while sparing normal bronchial epithelial cells. Low-dose PDT induces a moderate oxidative stress response, leading to DNA damage and G2/M cell cycle arrest. Importantly, this treatment triggers a senescence-associated phenotype, evidenced by increased SA-β-Gal activity and elevated secretion of SASP factors (IL-6, IL-8), accompanied by altered p53/GADD45 A signaling. These effects are abrogated by ROS scavenging or p53 inhibition, indicating that the oxidative response plays a central role in the observed antitumor activity. In the subcutaneous xenograft model, this regimen significantly suppresses tumor growth with no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work identifies BL-DVDMS-mediated PDT as a mechanistically defined, senescence-associated therapeutic strategy. This study provides a potential complementary treatment option for inoperable LC patients, particularly for managing residual disease and enhancing existing therapies.

papers.abstract_en: Although platinum sensitivity remains a convenient way to categorize relapsed small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), it no longer captures the full range of factors that may influence response to newer treatments. The interval to relapse still carries useful clinical information because it reflects the initial response, the pace of disease, and the emergence of resistance. It does not, however, identify whether a relapsed tumor can support checkpoint blockade, be efficiently recognized by a T-cell engager, or support delivery and respond to an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). This Review considers treatment vulnerability through five interconnected features: lineage plasticity, antigen-presentation competence, T-cell function, surface-target availability, and susceptibility to the delivered payload. We integrate clinical and translational findings for DLL3-directed T-cell engagers, B7-H3-directed ADCs, and SEZ6-directed ADCs, emphasizing that resistance may arise from the target, the immune effector compartment, or the payload. We then introduce a Time-Immune-Target framework. Time represents relapse kinetics; Immune denotes the functional capacity to mount or redirect an antitumor immune response; and Target denotes the accessibility of a therapeutically relevant surface antigen. Prior therapy is superimposed on these dimensions as a record of evolutionary pressure. This proposal is intended to guide hypothesis development, not current treatment assignment. Its clinical value will need to be tested prospectively using serial tissue and blood sampling, imaging, and formal biomarker-by-treatment interaction analyses.

papers.title_zh: Reproducibility of Lung Densitometry with Photon-counting Detector and Energy-integrating Detector CT: A Multi-Institutional Phantom Study.
papers.title_en: Reproducibility of Lung Densitometry with Photon-counting Detector and Energy-integrating Detector CT: A Multi-Institutional Phantom Study.
papers.authors: Sotoudeh-Paima S, O'Doherty J, Humphries SM, Atha J, McIntosh MJ, Sieren JC, Bache ST, Abadia A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Center for Virtual Imaging Trials, Carl E.
papers.abstract_en: Purpose To identify accurate imaging protocols for energy-integrating detector (EID) CT and photon-counting detector (PCD) CT, to establish comparable protocols across systems, and to evaluate the reproducibility of lung densitometry across body sizes, sites, and dose levels. Materials and Methods A chest phantom and a multidiameter phantom were scanned across four academic medical centers with PCD CT and EID CT systems across three doses. PCD CT included standard-resolution and ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) acquisitions with low-energy threshold (T3D) and virtual monoenergetic image (VMI) reconstructions, whereas EID CT used filtered back projection. Soft and sharp body and quantitative kernels were evaluated. Optimal protocols minimized mean absolute error (MAE) from reference CT attenuation values. Comparable protocols were identified using the histogram similarity index (HSI) within the lung sample (chest phantom), and reproducibility was assessed using air-insert density measurements. Statistical analyses included a Gaussian linear mixed-effects model and nonparametric tests for reproducibility. Results PCD CT outperformed both EID CT systems (P < .05) across 7392 measurements, achieving a lower MAE (3.7 HU ± 3.7 [SD]) than EID CT1 (6.4 HU ± 4.0; P < .05) and EID CT2 (12.4 HU ± 9.7; P < .05). The optimal PCD CT protocol used the UHR mode, high-dose, standard-resolution VMI, and soft quantitative reconstructions. Protocol matching across scanners was feasible, yielding an HSI of 95.6% ± 1.2 under optimal settings. Compared with EID CT, PCD CT exhibited greater reproducibility across body sizes (<2.2 HU), across sites (<2.5 HU), across dose levels (<3.9 HU), and within dose levels (<2.5 HU). Conclusion PCD CT provided more accurate and reproducible lung densitometry while maintaining comparability with EID CT protocols. Keywords: Phantom Studies, CT, CT-Photon Counting, CT-Quantitative, Thorax, Lung, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, Comparative Studies, Technology Assessment, Physics Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

papers.abstract_en: COVID-19 has disproportionately affected vulnerable populations worldwide; yet, data on SARS-CoV-2 transmission and variant diversity in Brazil's descendants of enslaved individuals, known as Quilombola, remain scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Cachoeira, Bahia, in people seeking care, between February and March 2021, testing 700 oropharyngeal swabs by RT-qPCR and 591 plasma samples for IgM/IgG antibodies. Positive samples with Cq < 25 underwent genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. SARS-CoV-2 infection burden was comparable between urban (31.4%) and rural (32.0%) zones in Quilombola communities. Genomic analysis of 39 sequences identified multiple lineages, predominantly the Gamma variant (P.1), with phylogenetic evidence of numerous introductions and both local and external transmission. These results reveal complex transmission dynamics and variant diversity within marginalized Quilombola populations, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions, expanded diagnostic coverage, and prioritization of these communities in vaccination campaigns to address health inequities.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: CD161 (KLRB1) is a C-type lectin-like immune receptor expressed on multiple immune-cell subsets and has context-dependent immunoregulatory functions. METHODS: We generated human anti-CD161 monoclonal antibodies, established a customized in-house sandwich ELISA for soluble CD161 (sCD161), and identified antibodies that block the CD161-LLT1 interaction. In a single-center cross-sectional cohort, we evaluated 63 untreated patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), together with 52 healthy controls (HCs), 6 patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), and 5 individuals with latent TB infection (LTBI) for plasma sCD161. Membrane CD161-positive cell frequencies were assessed in 57 TB patients and 27 HCs. CD161 distribution in lung and lymph-node tissues and the effects of CD161-LLT1 blockade on cytokine responses in an ESAT6-CFP10 antigen-stimulated PBMC system were also examined. RESULTS: Plasma sCD161 levels were higher in TB patients, particularly those classified as severe by radiographic criteria, and showed weak inverse associations with selected membrane CD161-positive T-cell frequencies. CD161 staining was increased in perigranulomatous regions and decreased in necrotic regions. Blocking CD161-LLT1 altered cytokine secretion, with reduced IFN-γ, IL-6, and TNF and increased IL-17A in selected antibody conditions. DISCUSSION: These findings indicate that circulating sCD161 is associated with TB and radiographic disease severity in this cohort, while CD161-LLT1 blockade modulates cytokine responses in an antigen-stimulated PBMC system. Larger, independently validated and longitudinal studies are required to determine the diagnostic and treatment-monitoring utility of sCD161 and to define the cellular mechanisms underlying CD161-LLT1 signaling in TB.
